title: Polarity flip of a literal encoding
statement: For every literal $\ell=(v,b)$ over variables indexed by $\mathbb{N}$ and every binary string $r$, scanning the encoding of $(v,b)$ followed by $r$ from the clause-level state produces the encoding of $(v,\neg b)$ followed by the scan of $r$ from the clause-level state.
hypotheses_covered: A literal with natural-number variable index and Boolean polarity
replaced:
For every literal $(v, b)$ and binary string $r$, the polarity-flipping scan from the
clause-level state of the formula syntax scanner maps the serialization of $(v, b)$
followed by $r$ to the serialization of $(v, \neg b)$ followed by the
polarity-flipping scan of $r$ from the clause-level state.
